title: SLO federation and priority-based adaptive load-shedding policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Define and publish an actionable SLO/SLI federation model that ties per-endpoint and per-model SLIs into composite SLOs, and pair it with a priority-aware adaptive load-shedding and circuit-breaker policy. Scope covers hosted and dedicated deployments across multi-region clusters; private/VPC rollout will be a follow-up. Deliverables: 1) SLO federation spec (how endpoint and model SLIs roll up to customer-facing SLOs), 2) priority classes and associated graceful degradation rules, 3) concrete circuit-breaker thresholds and adaptive load-shedding algorithm, 4) runbook and operator playbook, 5) observability and dashboards for SLO attribution and error-budget burn tracking, 6) test plan and staged rollout checklist.
acceptance_criteria: A clear schema for per-endpoint and per-model SLIs (latency percentiles, availability, correctness) with mapping rules into composite SLOs
Definition of at least three traffic priority classes (critical, standard, best-effort) with explicit degradation actions for each
Adaptive load-shedding algorithm documented: inputs (error budget delta, queue depth, CPU/GPU contention, regional latency), decision frequency, and backoff behavior
Circuit-breaker thresholds defined for per-route and per-model variants, with automatic recovery windows and humanoid-safe alerts
Runbook covering manual override, traffic reclassification, and multi-region failover steps validated by tabletop exercise
Dashboards and alerting configured for error-budget burn rate, per-priority dropped-requests, and end-to-end SLO attribution
Canary rollout executed in one non-prod cluster and one low-traffic production region with no customer-visible regression
notes: This ticket synthesizes previous SLO efforts but intentionally moves away from monolithic per-endpoint SLOs toward a federated model that allows model-variant weighting and customer-tier prioritization. It should reduce blast radius during cross-model regressions and provide deterministic fallback behavior.

runbook: Operator runbook (summary): 1) Detect burn pattern: alert fires on sustained >50% error-budget burn over 15m for composite SLO. 2) Verify region health and model variant metrics (p99 latency, kv-cache hit rate, GPU saturation). 3) If burn confirmed, escalate to 'temporary priority reclassification' and enable adaptive load-shedding in observation mode for 5m. 4) If dropped-request rate for critical class >0.1% or p99 remains >2x baseline, trigger regional circuit-breaker and initiate cross-region failover for critical routes. 5) Notify PM/Customer Success for impacted customers and create incident. 6) Use rollback or manual cool-down if error-budget burn reduces below 20% over 30m. Full steps, commands, and runbook links are in the Confluence page listed above.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): unit and chaos tests for the algorithm; validate metrics emission. Phase 1 (canary): enable in staging and one low-traffic prod region for best-effort + background classes only. Phase 2 (limited prod): enable for standard class in a single region with monitoring and automated rollback. Phase 3 (enterprise): enable critical class protections with customer opt-in for emergency failover. Each phase requires sign-off from SRE lead and PM and a post-mortem if any customer-visible errors occur.
observability_changes: New metrics to emit: slo_federation.composite_error_budget_burn, load_shed.dropped_requests_by_priority, circuitbreaker.open_count_by_route, model_variant.kv_cache_miss_rate, per_region.p99_latency. Dashboards for attribution and per-priority impact must be added. Alerts: urgent on composite error-budget burn >50% sustained for 15m; warn on dropped requests growth >50% minute-over-minute.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for SLO rollup logic and weighting. 2) Integration tests simulating model regressions and KV-cache thrashing. 3) Chaos tests that saturate GPU and network on one region while verifying cross-region failover. 4) Tabletop exercise with SRE, PM, Support on 2026-03-16. 5) Canary performance regression tests comparing p50/p95/p99 and correctness metrics before/after enablement.

implementation_notes: Adaptive algorithm uses proportional shedding by priority: when error-budget burn is high, compute target shed_ratio = clamp( (burn_rate - baseline) / scaling_factor, 0, 0.6 ). Drop best-effort traffic first, then background tasks; standard traffic is shed only under severe operations or if GPU saturation >85%. Circuit-breakers use multi-criterion open policy: p99 latency > 3x baseline OR error rate > 0.5% for 5m AND queue depth > threshold. Recovery uses exponential backoff with jitter. All threshold constants are tunable via runtime config and feature flags.
